run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Social Network
Namespace: social-network

A social network with unidirectional follow relationships, implemented with loosely-coupled microservices, communicating with each other via Thrift RPCs.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The social-network front door is broken: Deployment social-network/nginx-thrift was patched at 23:11:41 and its nginx-thrift container now runs with a 256Mi memory limit; that container has been OOMKilled (exit code 137) and is in CrashLoopBackOff with 4 restarts on pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-xcczg, so the nginx-thrift Service has no ready endpoint. All other 26 pods in the namespace are Ready with 0 restarts, node conditions show no memory pressure, and sampled Jaeger spans from 23:11:43-23:11:51 show HTTP 200 responses with ~1-15ms durations through compose-post-service, home-timeline-service, user-timeline-service and social-graph-service, so the backend microservices were not the failing layer. The user-visible effect appears in the wrk2 load generator: the interval ending 23:11:52 did 1021 requests (102.07 req/s, 3 socket write errors), while the interval ending 23:12:03 did only 129 requests (12.89 req/s, 4141 socket write errors, 12 timeouts). Counterevidence: the first pod from the patched ReplicaSet (nginx-thrift-65f656c999-mcjzj) served the 102 req/s interval successfully and was then deleted at 23:11:54 without a recorded Evicted/OOM/probe event, so the exact reason for that replacement is unknown and the memory limit did not break the container instantly. Conclusion is partial because no memory-usage series exists for this namespace, the declared fault's timing cannot be tied to the kubectl-patch beyond the template diff and manager timestamp, and no pre-restart latency baseline exists.

claims.text: In namespace social-network, 26 pods are Running with Ready=True and ContainersReady=True and 0 restarts, while pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-xcczg has Ready=False and ContainersReady=False with its nginx-thrift container ready=false and restarts=4.

Pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-xcczg shows the nginx-thrift container in state waiting/CrashLoopBackOff ("back-off 1m20s restarting failed container=nginx-thrift"), restartCount 4, and lastState.terminated reason OOMKilled with exitCode 137 (startedAt 2026-11-23T23:13:40Z, finishedAt 23:13:45Z).

The nginx-thrift Deployment's current pod template sets the nginx-thrift container to resources.limits.memory=256Mi and resources.requests.memory=128Mi with no CPU limits and no liveness or readiness probe.

Two ReplicaSets exist for nginx-thrift: nginx-thrift-68bc7d94df (created 2026-11-23T23:11:34Z, replicas 0) whose container resources are empty {}, and nginx-thrift-65f656c999 (created 23:11:41Z, replicas 1) whose container carries limits.memory=256Mi and requests.memory=128Mi, so the memory limit arrived with the newer ReplicaSet.

Deployment nginx-thrift is at generation 2 with annotation deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=2, and its managedFieldsSummary lists helm Apply at 2026-11-23T23:11:32Z and a kubectl-patch Update at 23:11:41Z (plus a kube-controller-manager status write).

Of the 27 Deployments in social-network, only nginx-thrift is at generation 2 with a kubectl-patch spec writer; every other Deployment is generation 1, last written by helm at 2026-11-23T23:11:32Z, so no other workload's pod template changed during the window.

nginx-thrift rollout events: ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-68bc7d94df created pod nginx-thrift-68bc7d94df-d6srj at 23:11:35Z and that pod was killed at 23:11:44Z; ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-65f656c999 created pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-mcjzj at 23:11:41Z, that pod was killed at 23:11:54Z, and pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-xcczg was created at 23:11:54Z on node sregym-worker.

The Endpoints object for Service nginx-thrift holds only notReadyAddresses for pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-xcczg (10.244.234.139 on sregym-worker) and no ready address, so the front-door Service has no ready backend.

The wrk2 load-generator pod's interval ending 23:11:52Z reported 1021 requests in 10.00s (Requests/sec 102.07) with 3 socket write errors, while the interval ending 23:12:03Z reported only 129 requests in 10.01s (Requests/sec 12.89) with 4141 socket write errors and 12 timeouts, against endpoint http://10.96.121.102:8080/wrk2-api/post/compose.

Sampled Jaeger spans from 23:11:43-23:11:51Z show nginx-web-server /wrk2-api/post/compose, /wrk2-api/home-timeline/read and /wrk2-api/user-timeline/read spans with http.status_code 200 and durations of about 0.7-15ms, with child spans in compose-post-service, home-timeline-service, user-timeline-service and social-graph-service.

In the window 23:11:30-23:12:04Z the notable namespace log lines besides the wrk2 socket-error report were startup-time MongoDB index-creation retries from user-service, post-storage-service, url-shorten-service and user-timeline-service and MongoDB NETWORK/TCP-FastOpen informatics; no backend runtime error line appeared after startup.

All four nodes (sregym-control-plane, sregym-worker, sregym-worker2, sregym-worker3) are Ready with MemoryPressure=False, DiskPressure=False, PIDPressure=False and about 32859952Ki allocatable memory each, so node-level memory pressure is not the cause of the container kill.

The 256Mi memory limit placed on the nginx-thrift container's pod template at 23:11:41Z is below what the openresty/Lua front door consumes under load, so the container exceeds the cgroup limit, is OOMKilled with exit 137 and enters CrashLoopBackOff; because this Service has no other pod, external API traffic through it fails, which matches the wrk2 throughput collapse from 102.07 to 12.89 req/s with 4141 write errors, while backend microservices stay healthy.

A backend microservice or database failure was considered as the cause and rejected: the 26 non-front-door pods are Ready with 0 restarts, all nodes report no pressure, the MongoDB connection errors at 23:11:33-23:11:37Z are startup index retries from freshly started pods, and sampled traces in the same period show HTTP 200 with millisecond latencies through compose-post-service, home-timeline-service, user-timeline-service and social-graph-service.

The first pod of the patched ReplicaSet, nginx-thrift-65f656c999-mcjzj, which carries the same 256Mi template, served the successful interval at 102.07 req/s during 23:11:43-23:11:51Z, and the throughput collapse appears only in the interval ending 23:12:03Z, after that pod was killed at 23:11:54Z and replaced, so the limit did not break the container immediately at startup.

Restore a workable memory budget for the nginx-thrift container (remove the 256Mi limit or raise it well above the container's real working set, keeping requests consistent) so the front-door pod stops being OOMKilled, and add readiness/liveness probes so a degraded front door is detected instead of silently dropping all endpoints.

gaps: Prometheus in this target has no series for namespace social-network (kube-state-metrics/cAdvisor cover only kube-system, local-path-storage, observe, openebs and sregym); queries for container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace="social-network",pod=~"nginx-thrift.*"} and kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason for that namespace returned no data, so no numeric usage curve versus the 256Mi limit and no pre-incident memory baseline exist; the memory conclusion rests on the OOMKilled/exit-137 termination reason plus the template limit.

The reason pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-mcjzj (same ReplicaSet, same 256Mi template) was deleted at 23:11:54Z is unknown: no Evicted, OOM or probe-failure event was recorded for it, so that particular replacement is unexplained.

The nginx-thrift container wrote no stdout/stderr lines retrievable through the pod-log tool (0 lines read for both current and previous instances), so no application-level crash or Lua error message was observed; only the Kubernetes termination reason is available.
Jaeger holds spans only from 23:11:43Z onward because Jaeger and the application pods restarted at 23:11:32-23:11:54Z, so there is no pre-restart latency baseline to compare against.

The authorized window ends 2026-11-23T23:12:04Z while the last observed OOMKill on nginx-thrift-65f656c999-xcczg is timestamped 23:13:45Z (object state read at query time); the pod's state at the exact end of the authorized window cannot be reconstructed from Prometheus because that namespace is not scraped.
Secrets could not be read: the service-config.json "secret" value and the SSL serverCertPath were redacted, so no conclusion depends on them and they were not verified.

Change history is not integrated in this Run, so what the 23:11:41Z kubectl-patch actually contained is inferred from the ReplicaSet template difference (resources {} versus limits.memory 256Mi) and the managedFieldsSummary timestamp, not from a change record.
Traces-search views were truncated/large (the 142-span result and the 27-ConfigMap result), so only the read slices cited were inspected; unread rows of those results remain unknown.
next_steps: Inspect and revert the kubectl-patch applied to Deployment social-network/nginx-thrift at 23:11:41Z (limits.memory 256Mi / requests.memory 128Mi) or raise the limit above the container's measured working set.
Enable cAdvisor/kube-state-metrics scraping for namespace social-network and measure the nginx-thrift container's RSS under the standard wrk2 post/compose load to size the limit correctly.
Add readiness and liveness probes to the nginx-thrift container and alert on nginx-thrift ready endpoint count = 0, since the front-door outage was visible only via load-generator socket errors.
Confirm whether nginx-thrift-65f656c999-mcjzj's deletion at 23:11:54Z came from an external pod-kill or eviction (no Evicted/OOM event was recorded) to rule out a second independent fault.
After remediation, replay the wrk2 post/compose workload and verify throughput returns near 102 req/s with zero socket write errors and no further OOMKilled terminations.
